the combinational probe is slower at a LOOSER target -- 280.7 MHz at 2.0 ns, 253.0 at 3.8, 247.1 at 4.2 -- because the optimiser works less hard when it has slack. The closed-to-closed ratio therefore uses the combinational side at its most favourable CLOSED point, not at its fastest measured path
question: on ONE design differing only in whether the FP32 multiply is pipelined, what does the construct cost?

result.statement: the pipelined form is 3.65x faster AND 2.38x smaller, so it is 8.68x better per unit area. Pipelining this construct does not trade area for speed -- it wins both.

why: the frequency audit compared ot_a3_vector_scale against the attention walks, which differ in this construct but are not otherwise the same design. These two probes are identical except for the multiply: same ports, same input and output registers, same corner, flow, utilisation and slew margin.
